2.34.m: 2.172 / The traversed minutes of the true sign of the sun at the desired time, multiplied by the respiration-periods (prāṇa) of the rising of that sign of the ecliptic, one should divide by the minutes of the sign. The quotient is the daytime portion of the sun's sign of the ecliptic. That is [subtracted] from the respiration-periods of the desired time, and the untraversed minutes of the sun are to be added; and at that time, referring to the subsequent rising of the sun […] ascensional difference and rising is to be given; from the remainder, by means of the unexhausted risings of the signs, the houses (bhāva) and so forth [are found]. / Thus the rising of the ascendant (lagna) for the elapsed time of the sign [is determined]. From the sun with six signs added are the times of the sun's traversed time and so forth; and the ascendants are from the traversed minutes; in their conjunction, the rising of the ascendant is the time when the difference is added to the rising.

2.34.m:
Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn [have] the anomaly [as] the quick [apogee/epicycle]; when retrograde, Mercury and Venus are slow, and otherwise quick. When the slow planet is situated between [itself] and the sun by degrees of visible and invisible time, then in the eastern half of rising and setting, the planet pertains to sunrise; by the western half, it pertains to sunset. One should divide the true celestial latitude of the planet for that time, multiplied by the sine of the slow [anomaly], by the radius.
From the result, [it is] subtractive for the rising planet, [and] additive for the setting one; one should divide by the maximum declination of northern latitude.
The obtained [value] should be subtracted from the other solstice-latitude, otherwise added.
Thus are the rising and setting ascendants of the planet.
Then, from the difference of the planets, as with the ascendant, is the time; one should divide the degree by the difference of the arms of the minutes and degrees of planetary difference.
When the planet is retrograde, by the sum of the motions the time in days and so forth of the setting is obtained; thus for the lunar mansions, their visible and invisible degrees are twelve. Having performed the two directional operations of the fixed star Canopus, one should increase [it] by its two ghaṭikās in the rising of the signs in one's own locality.
In that degree is the rising of Canopus; when retrograde, the setting. The daily rising up to the planet is by virtue of the ascendant.

लब्धेग्रे क्रान्तिदिष्टेशेन ततोर्कचन्द्रशंकुकार्यौ पृथक्च्छंकुहताक्षज्यावलम्बकेन विभजेत् ।
लब्धे शङ्कुतले तौ चोत्तरे स्वरात्रौ दिवसयाम्ये द्वादशशंकुतलयोर्दिशैको योगो दिग्भेदवियोगः पृथग्बाहुः तयोर्दिगैको वियोगोन्यथा योगःस्फुटबाहुः स्वदृगर्ण्यवर्जभुजावर्गविश्लेषपदयोगः कपालभेदे साम्ये वियोगः प्रथमांशजां दिगैवातिश्लेषो दिग्भेदो युतिर्द्वितीयः प्रथमद्वितीयवर्गयोगपदं कोटिः कोटि वाहुवर्गयोगमूलकर्णः अर्कोनाश्चन्द्रार्केर्द्धं तस्माज्ज्याकेन्द्रलिप्ताश्चन्द्रमासलिप्ताः तस्माज्ज्याकेन्द्रलिप्ताश्चन्द्रमानघ्नाः नवत्याहृतास्मिन् केन्द्र प्रयमचतुर्थपदस्थे द्वितीयस्थे कृष्णम् इन्दुमानचतुर्भागकृतास्मितेर्कमानभुजककर्णकोटिसूत्राण्यङ्गुलतां यान्ति पूर्वापराशाभिमुखार्केन्द्राण्याद्य पदगे मितशृङ्गं परिलिखेत् ।
एवं द्वितीयतृतीयगे कृष्णं बिन्दुमर्कं परिकल्प्य ततोर्काद्यथा शशी तथा भुजा देया तदग्रात्स्वाभिमुख्येन कोटिः ततः तदंतलग्नेन पूर्वान्तं पुनःपुनः सत्कुलम् ।
यावदविशेषं लब्धोनं स्यात् इति लम्बनं संस्कृते तिथ्यन्ते ग्रहणमध्यश्चन्द्रश्चन्द्रवत्कल्पिताद्द्वित्रि भात्स्वक्रान्तिः अक्षे सौम्या शोध्या याम्या देया तज्ज्यामध्यमचन्द्रार्कभुक्त्यंतरहता शरेर्कहतया त्रिज्यया विभजेत् ।
लब्धभवनतिः स्वक्रान्तितोक्षेधिके सौम्यान्यथा याम्या तात्कालिकचन्द्रविक्षेपावनन्यादिगैक्ये योगो दिग्भेदो वियोगः स्फुटविक्षेपः तेन स्थिते मन्दभदलोनयुतैर्ग्रहैः स्पर्थनिमीलोन्मीलनमोक्षकालिकैलम्बनमानि कार्याणि मध्यलम्बनस्येष्टलंबनस्य धनर्णेकोन्तरे भेदयोगः फलम् ।
तेन मध्यस्थित्यरविमन्दावेव युते स्वकालिके स्फुटे भवतः पञ्चदशं घटिकाकालिकं लंबने फलेन हीने विमंदार्धे कार्ये शेषं पीरलेखाढ्ये चद्रग्रहणवद्भवति ॥
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्गलोकप्रदं तथा ॥
इदं ग्रहाणां गणितं सर्वकामप्रदं शिवम् ॥
गतिमेकस्य विज्ञाय ग्रहस्य सुसमाहितः ॥

2.34.m:
The rising and setting ascendants of the sun and the moon are their own; from that, the times of rising and setting of the moon are to be determined. One should divide [the sine of] the sun's and moon's own declination at the desired time, multiplied by the radius, by its own sine [of the diurnal circle].
The results being the amplitude in the direction of the declination, then the gnomons of the sun and the moon are to be made; one should divide separately the sine of latitude multiplied by the gnomon by the equinoctial gnomon/colatitude.
The results being the base of the gnomons, those two are in the north in their own night, [and] in the south by day. If the directions of the bases of the twelve[-finger] gnomons are the same, there is addition; if the directions differ, subtraction: [this is] the separate base. If their directions are the same, subtraction; otherwise, addition: [this is] the corrected base. The square root of the difference between the squares of the base and its own visibility is added when the hemispheres differ; when identical, there is subtraction. The direction arising from the first part is difference; when directions differ, it is sum; the second, the square root of the sum of the squares of the first and second is the upright; the square root of the sum of the squares of the upright and base is the hypotenuse. Subtracting the sun from the moon's and sun's [distance] is half; from that, the sine of the minutes of anomaly are the minutes of the lunar month. From that, the sine of the minutes of anomaly multiplied by the moon's measure, divided by ninety: when situated in the first and fourth quadrant of this anomaly, [it is bright]; when situated in the second, dark. The cords of the base, hypotenuse, and upright made into a fourth part of the moon's measure reach the state of inches. With the anomaly of the sun and moon facing the eastern and western quarters, when situated in the first quadrant, one should delineate the measured cusp.
Thus, when situated in the second and third, conceiving the black dot as the sun, then the base is to be placed as the moon is from the sun; from its tip, facing oneself, the upright. Then, by the ascendant at its end, the eastern limit repeatedly, well-calculated,
until it becomes identical without difference. Thus, parallax in longitude having been corrected at the end of the lunar day, the middle of the eclipse [occurs]. The moon's own declination is from two or three signs conceived like the moon; north in the latitude is to be subtracted, south to be added; that sine multiplied by the difference between the mean motions of the moon and sun, multiplied by the arrow and the sun, one should divide by the radius.
The result is parallax in latitude. If latitude is greater than its own declination, it is north; otherwise south. If the contemporaneous lunar latitude has the same direction as the other, there is addition; if different directions, subtraction: [this is] the corrected latitude. By that, with the planets increased or decreased by half the duration of the eclipse, the parallax values at the times of first contact, total obscuration, beginning of emergence, and completion of release are to be calculated. The difference between the addition and subtraction of the middle parallax and the desired parallax is the result.
By that, the two [times] of half the middle duration, combined with the sun and slow [planet], become corrected for their own time. When fifteen ghaṭikās are decreased by the result in parallax at that time, they are to be made into half the duration; the remainder, filled with the eclipse-diagram, is like a lunar eclipse.
This calculation of the planets brings fortune, brings renown, grants long life, and bestows the world of heaven; it grants all desires and is auspicious.
Having understood the motion of a single planet, deeply concentrated,
one attains that planet's realm; no doubt should be entertained here.
Having understood the motion of all the planets, one reaches the world of Brahmā.
One who seeks dharma will obtain dharma; one who seeks wealth will obtain wealth;
one who has desires will obtain desires; one who seeks liberation will obtain the supreme abode.
Having fully understood the motion of the planets, a twice-born person truly becomes worthy of gifts;
if he does not make a living by it, he should thus abandon [such] livelihood;
he who knows the motion of the planets is the most worthy among worthy recipients.
The Vedas are indeed undertaken for the sake of sacrifice, and sacrifices are prescribed in accordance with the divisions of time;
therefore, this scripture of the ordinances of time—he who knows astronomy knows everything.
Thus ends the one hundred and seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Paitāmaha Siddhānta', in the Second Book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya [and Vajra].

2.34.m: 2.166 / Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then Rāma, descendant of Bhṛgu, asked Puṣkara, the son of Varuṇa: / "O venerable one, I wish to hear the science of astronomy and astrology." / Varuṇa's son said to him: / "Formerly, Bhṛgu made a request to the lord, the foremost creator, protector, and destroyer of the whole universe, the illustrious Brahmā, who was seated amidst a host of gods and celestial seers: / 'O venerable one, I wish to hear the course of the celestial luminaries.' / The venerable Grandfather said to him: / 'When you were born from my heart at the beginning of the aeon, I taught you the course of the celestial luminaries in twenty-four hundred thousand verses; that very same [teaching] I will declare to you in extreme brevity, since you were born in another birth after issuing forth through the flame by the curse of Mahādeva in this sacrifice of Varuṇa. / Hearing that, all the knowledge of the celestial luminaries declared to you in your previous birth will manifest.' / Now, the thousand-rayed lord [the Sun], pure with clear rays, brings welfare; [when] shaped like a peacock's feather, [it is suited] for grasping praise; the Moon, visible like the moon, [leads] to the acquisition of a kingdom; and in a planetary conjunction, if the Moon is seen situated to the north and in the middle. / And in a conjunction of asterisms, asterisms and the like are also praised according to circumstances. / Now, from the asterism in which Mars rises, in the seventh, eighth, and ninth asterisms, he makes an opening called 'Pūṣan's Face', by which fire-worshipping brahmins and those who live by fire are afflicted. / In the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth, he makes [one] called 'Horse's Face', causing pestilence. / In the thirteenth and fourteenth, [he makes one] called 'Beast's Face', causing an increase in beasts of prey. / In the fifteenth and sixteenth, [he makes] 'Blood Face', portending battle. / In the seventeenth and eighteenth, [he makes] 'Sword Face', causing the predominance of thieves. / Now, Mercury, moving in Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, and Rohiṇī, moves with the natural course that produces abundance of food.

2.34.m: In Āśleṣā, Ārdrā, and Maghā, [he moves with] the mixed [course], granting mixed fruit; in Punarvasu, Puṣya, Pūrvaphālgunī, and Uttaraphālgunī, [he moves with] the shortened [course], likewise granting mixed fruit; in [the asterisms] named Uttarabhādrapadā, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Revatī, Jyeṣṭhā, and Kṛttikā, [he moves with] the sharp [course], causing conflict; through connection with the triad beginning with Mūla, [he moves with the course] granting radiance, fame, and the like; in Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣaj, and Citrā, [he moves with] the terrible [course], bearing terrible fruit. / Jupiter, moving through a zodiacal sign in thirteen months, is auspicious; otherwise, his fruit is difficult. / Now, by the movements of rising and setting of Venus: the first circle of four asterisms beginning with Bharaṇī produces abundance of food; the four beginning with Ārdrā also brings fear to the twice-born; the five asterisms beginning with Jyeṣṭhā produces disease; the six asterisms beginning with Dhaniṣṭhā causes excessive rain. / In whichever asterisms of a country, commodity, or person Saturn moves, many afflictions befall them. / In whichever direction the tail of a comet is blazing, in that direction the king should attack. / An eclipse of Rāhu that is white, red, yellow, or black causes affliction to brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras [respectively]. / Agastya, [if] trembling and summoned by dryness, resembling the crest of a peacock, [is] for fear. / Such also are the Seven Seers; when they are such, even the threefold world is afflicted. In the north-eastern direction, Kumāra rises together with the Pleiades; when he is such, there is affliction to children. / Jupiter, Mercury, and Saturn are city planets. / Mars and Venus are marching planets. / The Moon and the Sun are intermediate. / There, planetary setting occurs in conjunction with the Sun. / Conjunction with the Moon is a mutual battle. / The planet that is gone to the northern path and is very bright becomes victorious. / When a marching planet is victorious and direct, the king should attack his enemies; otherwise, when the city planets are strong, destruction of the marching [attackers] would occur. / When an asterism is afflicted like Agastya, affliction occurs to the country, commodity, and person born of it. / Or, in whichever direction the earthquake goes, to that direction the king should march. / If it is accompanied by a thunderous crash and is prolonged, there would be the death of the king. / In whichever direction a meteor goes, to that direction the king should march.

दिवोल्का चन्द्रार्कविनिर्गता उद्धातिन्यतिस्थूला सस्फुलिङ्गा ततोर्ध्वगा राजमृत्यवे स्यात् ।
बहुवर्णे परिवेषे प्रजापीडा स्यात्, यतः खण्डः परिवेषः स्यात्, तां दिशं नृपतिर्यायात् ।
अतिभीमनिर्घातो राजमृत्यवे ।
यां च दिशं याति तां दिशं राजा यायात् ।
गन्धर्वनगरं शक्योद्भूतं महाभयाय ।
रात्राविन्द्रधनुः श्वेतं व्यभ्रे च महाभयाय ।
प्रतिसूर्यं उदग्दक्षिणेनार्काद्वातकृत् ।
उभयस्थितो महावर्षाय उपरि राजमृत्यवे ॥
तथाधस्ताज्जनविनाशाय ।
उभयथा महाभयाय सर्वतः त्रिभुवनपीडावहो भवति ।
या दिग्दाहेन दीप्ता स्यात्तां दिशं राजा यायात् ।
अतिदीप्ते छायाव्यञ्जके राजमरणं विन्द्यात् ॥
अथ वा ध्रुवदारुणोग्रक्षिप्रचरसाधारणेषु यथा स्वकर्म ध्रुवादिकर्म क्रियमाणं सिद्धिमुपैति ॥ व्यतीपातविष्टिवैधृतास्तमितनक्षत्रेषु न किञ्चिदपि ।
तथा चार्कानलराहुधूमितज्वलितदग्धविद्धेषु नक्षत्रेषु तथा च विविधोत्पाताभिहतेषु यत्र यस्मिन्नक्षत्रे पुरुषस्य जन्म तन्नक्षत्रं तस्मान्नक्षत्राच्च दशमं तत एकोनविंशज्जन्मनक्षत्रमिति विन्द्यात् ।
(सर्वस्माज्जन्मनक्षत्राद्द्वितीयं संपत्करम् ।
तृतीयं विपत्करं ।
चतुर्थ क्षेम्यम् ।
पञ्चमं प्रत्यरि ।
षष्ठं साधकम् ।
सप्तमं नैधनम् ।
अष्टमं मैत्रम् ।
नवमं परमं मैत्रं चेति)॥
तत्र सम्पत्करक्षेमसाधक मैत्रातिमैत्रेषु सर्वाणि कर्माणि कुर्यात् ।
दशमर्क्षे च ॥
यथा कर्मसु नक्षत्रे तिथिं रिक्तां विना कृतम्॥
सौम्ये दिनकृते वत्स सिद्धिमायात्यसंशयम्॥
2.34.m: A daytime meteor emerging from the Moon or the Sun, striking upwards, extremely thick, accompanied by sparks, and moving upwards from there, would be for the death of the king. / When a halo is multicolored, there would be affliction of the subjects; whichever direction the halo is broken, to that direction the king should march. / An exceedingly terrifying thunderous crash is for the death of the king. / And in whichever direction it goes, in that direction the king should march. / A city of the gandharvas that appears is for great fear. / A white rainbow at night and in a cloudless sky is for great fear. / A mock sun to the north and south of the Sun causes wind; / standing on both sides, it causes heavy rain; above, it is for the death of the king; / likewise, below, it causes the destruction of the people; / on both sides, it brings great fear everywhere and brings affliction to the three worlds. / Whichever direction is illuminated by the burning of the horizon, in that direction the king should march. / When it is exceedingly bright, showing shadows, one should know it portends the death of the king. / Or rather, in [asterisms classified as] fixed, cruel, fierce, swift, movable, and common, work of a fixed nature and the like, performed appropriately according to each kind, attains success; in [asterisms connected with] Vyatīpāta, Viṣṭi, Vaidhṛta, or in set asterisms, none at all. / And so in asterisms that are smoked, blazed, burnt, or struck by the Sun, fire, or Rāhu, and similarly afflicted by various portents: the asterism in which a person is born is his birth asterism, and from that asterism the tenth, and from that the nineteenth, is to be known as a birth asterism. / From every birth asterism: the second brings prosperity; / the third brings misfortune; / the fourth brings welfare; / the fifth is inimical; / the sixth brings accomplishment; / the seventh brings death; / the eighth brings friendship; / and the ninth brings supreme friendship. / There, in [asterisms that are] prosperity-bringing, welfare-bringing, accomplishing, friendly, and exceedingly friendly, one should perform all undertakings, / and in the tenth asterism. / Performed in an asterism suitable to the actions, avoiding an empty lunar day, / on a day made auspicious and ruled by a gentle [planet], my child, it undoubtedly attains success.

2.167
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
अथ ब्रह्माणं भगवंतं भृगुर्विज्ञापयामास भगवञ्ज्ञातुमुडुचक्रमिच्छामि ।
तमुवाच भगवान् ।
वत्स द्वादशराशयो भचक्रम् ।
त्रिंशद्भागाश्च राशेः ।
षष्टिः लिप्तश्च भागः ।
षष्टिर्विलिप्ताश्च लिप्ता षष्टिः परा विलिप्ता ।
षष्टिश्च नाडिका अहोरात्रम् ।
षष्टिर्विनाडिका।
नाडिका तत्र यः काले प्राणः सा क्षेत्रे लिप्ता ।
तस्माद्यावता कालेन प्राणो भवति ।
दशगुर्वक्षरलक्षणस्तावता कालेन भचक्रस्यैका कलाभ्युदेति ।
सकलं भचक्रं नाडिकाषष्ट्येति तत्रादावेव राशिरजो रक्तवर्णः कालस्यमूर्धा (पूर्वावन्यो) दिवारात्रौ ग्राम्यः प्राग्द्वारः चतुष्पात् रात्रौ दक्षिणस्यां दिशि बली चरः पृष्ठोदयः क्रूरो विषमः पुमाञ् शनैश्चरस्य नीचः । विंशतिस्तथागतस्यैवातिनीचः ।
आदित्यस्योच्चः, तस्यैव दशमे भागेऽत्युच्चः अङ्गारक्षेत्रम् ।
तस्यैव त्रिकोणमिति ॥
वृषः श्वेतवर्णो मुखं कालस्यारण्यो दिवारात्रौ ग्राम्यो दक्षिणद्वारः चतुष्पाद्रात्रौ दक्षिणस्यां दिशि बली स्थिरः पृष्ठोदयः समः सौम्यः स्त्रीराशिः शुक्रक्षेत्रं चन्द्रमसस्त्रिकोणं तस्यैव च तृतीये भागे चात्युच्चमिति ॥
मिथुनः पुरुषो गदाधारी वीणाकरा नारी च हरितवर्णः कालस्य बाहू ग्राम्यः पश्चिमद्वारो द्विपात् पूर्वस्यां दिशि दिवा बली द्विस्वभावः शीर्षोदयः क्रूरो विषमः पुरुषराशिः बुधक्षेत्रमिति ॥
बली चरः पृष्ठोदयः कीटः सौम्यः समः स्त्रीराशिः चन्द्रक्षेत्रं भौमनीचः तस्याष्टविंशत्तमे भागेऽतिनीचो जीवोच्चस्तस्य पञ्चमे भागेऽत्युच्च इति ॥
सिंहः सिंहाकारः पाण्डुवर्णः कालस्योदरमारण्यः प्राग्द्वारः चतुष्पात् दक्षिणस्यां दिशि रात्रौ बली स्थिरः शीर्षोदयः
2.34.m:
2.167
Puṣkara said:
Then Bhṛgu requested the blessed Brahmā: "O Blessed One, I wish to know the wheel of the lunar asterisms."
The Blessed One said to him:
"Child, the wheel of asterisms consists of twelve signs.
And thirty degrees [make up] a sign.
And sixty minutes [make up] a degree.
And sixty seconds [make up] a minute; sixty thirds [make up] a second.
And sixty nāḍikās [make up] a day and night.
Sixty vināḍikās [make up a nāḍikā].
There, that which is a breath in time corresponds to a minute in space.
Therefore, in the amount of time in which a breath occurs—
defined as ten long syllables—in that much time, one minute of the wheel of asterisms rises.
The entire wheel of asterisms [rises] in sixty nāḍikās. There, at the very beginning, the sign is the Ram: red-colored, the head of Time, wild by day and domestic by night, facing east, four-footed, strong at night in the southern direction, movable, rising by the back, cruel, odd, male, the debilitation of Saturn—at twenty [degrees] thus reached is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of the Sun, and at his tenth degree is his deep exaltation, the domicile of Mars, and his trine.
The Bull: white-colored, the face of Time, wild by day and domestic by night, facing south, four-footed, strong at night in the southern direction, fixed, rising by the back, even, gentle, a female sign, the domicile of Venus, the trine of the Moon, and at its third degree is its deep exaltation.
The Twins: a man holding a club and a woman holding a lute, green-colored, the arms of Time, domestic, facing west, two-footed, strong in the eastern direction by day, dual-natured, rising by the head, cruel, odd, a male sign, the domicile of Mercury.
[The Crab] strong, movable, rising by the back, a creature, gentle, even, a female sign, the domicile of the Moon, the debilitation of Mars—at its twenty-eighth degree is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of Jupiter, and at his fifth degree is his deep exaltation.
The Lion: of leonine form, pale-colored, the belly of Time, wild, facing east, four-footed, strong in the southern direction at night, fixed, rising by the head,

2.34.d:
क्रूरो विषमः पुमान् आदित्यक्षेत्रं तत्त्रिकोणमिति ॥
कन्याराशिः कुमारी नौस्था दीपिकाहस्ता विचित्रवर्णा कालस्य कटिः ग्राम्यो दक्षिणद्वारः पूर्वस्यां दिशि बली स्थिरः शीर्षोदयः समः सौम्यः स्त्रीराशिः शुक्रस्य नीचः सप्तविंशतितमे भागे तस्यैवातिनीचो बुधस्योच्चस्तस्य पञ्चदशे भागेऽत्युच्चो बुधक्षेत्रं तत्त्रिकोणमिति ॥
तुला वणिक् पुरुषः तुलाधरापणवीथीगतः कृष्णवर्णः कालस्य वस्तिस्थितो ग्राम्यः पश्चिमद्वारो द्विधा पूर्वस्यां दिशि बली चरः शीर्षोदयः क्रूरो विषमः पुरुषराशिः शुक्रक्षेत्रम् आदित्यनीचस्तस्यैव दशमे भागेऽतिनीचः शनैश्चरस्योच्चश्चोर्ध्वः तस्यैव विंशतितमे भागेऽत्युच्चः तस्यैवातिनीचो भौमक्षेत्रमिति॥
धन्वीनाम धनुर्धरः पुरुषो हयपश्चिमार्धः पिङ्गलः कालस्योरू ग्राम्यः प्राग्द्वारः तस्य प्रागर्धो द्विपात्, द्वितीयमर्धं चतुष्पात् तस्य प्रथममर्धं पूर्वस्यां दिशि दिवाबली पश्चिमान्तमर्धं रात्रौ दक्षिणस्यां दिशि बलवान्, द्विस्वभावः पृष्ठोदयः क्रूरः पुमान्विषमो जीवक्षेत्रं तत्त्रिकोणमिति ॥
मकरो नाम मृगः पूवार्धो मकरः, पश्चार्धो मृगः, प्रागर्धेनारण्यो द्वितीयार्धेनाम्बुचरः (कबेरैः) कालस्य जानुनी पूर्वार्धोर्धचतुष्पात्, पश्चार्धेन कीटो, दक्षिणद्वारः, प्रागर्धेन रात्रौ दक्षिणस्यां दिशि बली पश्चिमार्धेन, सन्ध्यायां पश्चिमायां दिशि चरः, नीचं बृहस्पतेः तस्यैव पश्चिमे भागेऽतिनीचं, भौमस्योच्चस्तस्यै वाष्टाविंशतितमे भागेऽत्युच्चः, सौरक्षेत्रमिति ॥
2.34.m:

The sign Maiden: a maiden seated in a boat holding a lamp in her hand, of variegated color, the waist of Time, domestic, facing south, strong in the eastern direction, fixed, rising by the head, even, gentle, a female sign, the debilitation of Venus—at the twenty-seventh degree is her deep debilitation—the exaltation of Mercury, and at his fifteenth degree is his deep exaltation, the domicile of Mercury, and his trine.
The Scales: a merchant man, carrying a balance and standing in a shop-lane, black-colored, situated at the bladder of Time, domestic, facing west, two-footed, strong in the eastern direction, movable, rising by the head, cruel, odd, a male sign, the domicile of Venus, the debilitation of the Sun—at his tenth degree is his deep debilitation—and the exaltation of Saturn, upwards; at his twentieth degree is his deep exaltation, [and] his deep debilitation, the domicile of Mars.
Bowman by name: a man holding a bow with the hind-half of a horse, tawny, the thighs of Time, domestic, facing east; its front half is two-footed, the second half is four-footed; its first half is strong in the eastern direction by day, the rear end half is strong in the southern direction at night, dual-natured, rising by the back, cruel, male, odd, the domicile of Jupiter, and his trine.
Makara by name, a beast: the front half is a makara, the hind half is a deer; by its front half it is wild, by its second half it is water-roaming; the knees of Time; with its front half it is four-footed in the upper part, with its hind half it is an aquatic creature, facing south; by its front half it is strong in the southern direction at night, by its hind half it is movable at twilight in the western direction; the debilitation of Jupiter—at its fifth degree is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of Mars, and at his twenty-eighth degree is his deep exaltation, the domicile of Saturn.

2.34.d:
कुम्भो नाम पुरुषः स्कन्धेन रिक्तकुम्भधरः पिङ्गलः कालस्य जंघे द्विपाद्ग्राम्यः पश्चिमद्वारः पूर्वेण च दिवा बली शीर्षोदयः स्थिरः क्रूरः पुमान्विषमः शनैश्चरक्षेत्रं तत्त्रिकोणमिति ॥
मीनो नाम द्वौ मत्स्यावन्योन्यपुच्छादिमुखौ मत्स्यवर्णौ कालपादौ कीट उदीचः पश्चिमस्यां दिशि सन्ध्यायां बली पृष्ठपुच्छोदयो दूस्वभावः सौम्यः समः स्त्रीराशिः बुधस्य नीचं तस्यैव बुधस्य पञ्चदशभागेऽतिनीचं शुक्रस्योच्चं तस्यैव सप्तविंशतितमे भागेऽत्युच्चं जीवक्षेत्रमिति ॥
सर्वस्यैव राशेरर्धं होरा तत्र विषमराशिषु प्रथमा प्रथमा सौरी द्वितीया चांद्री समराशिषु चान्द्री द्वितीया सौरी सर्वराशिषु द्रेष्काणत्रयम् । ते प्रथमपञ्चमनवमराशिनाथाः ।
प्राग्द्वाराणां राशीनां मेषाद्या न वांशकाः दक्षिणद्वाराणां मकराद्याः पश्चिमद्वाराणां तुलाद्याः उत्तरद्वाराणां कुलीराद्याः सर्वादिर्यो नवांशको वर्गोत्तमः कर्कटवृश्चिकमीनानां चरमांशा गण्डान्ताः॥
राशौ राशौ द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां द्वादशद्वादशभागाः ।
त्रिंशाशंकाः पञ्च भौमस्य, ततः पञ्च सौरस्य, ततोऽष्टौ जीवस्य, सप्त बुधस्याष्टौ भृगोर्विषमे राशौ, समराशौ तु अष्टौ शुक्रस्य ततः सप्त बुधस्य ततोऽष्टौ जीवस्य पञ्च सौरस्य पञ्च भौमस्येति॥
एवं षट्पदार्थो लग्नः स स्वस्वामिना जीवेन बुधेन शुक्रेण वा युक्तो दृष्टो बलवान्भवति ।
शेषैर्मुक्तो दृष्टो हीनबलः स्यात् ।
एवं च राशिं सप्तमस्थो ग्रहः सर्वदृष्ट्या पश्यति॥।
चतुर्थाष्टमयोश्च स्थिताः पादा नेया दृष्ट्या पञ्चमनवमयोश्चार्धदृष्ट्या ।
तृतीयदशमयोश्च पाददृष्ट्या एक, द्वि, अष्ट, द्वादशे स्थितो न पश्यतीति॥
2.34.m:
Water-pot by name: a man carrying an empty water-pot on his shoulder, tawny, the shanks of Time, two-footed, domestic, facing west, and strong in the east by day, rising by the head, fixed, cruel, male, odd, the domicile of Saturn, and his trine.
Fishes by name: two fish with each other's tail facing the mouth, fish-colored, the feet of Time, aquatic creatures of the north, strong in the western direction at twilight, rising by the back and tail, dual-natured, gentle, even, a female sign, the debilitation of Mercury—at the fifteenth degree of that very Mercury is his deep debilitation—the exaltation of Venus, and at her twenty-seventh degree is her deep exaltation, the domicile of Jupiter.
Half of every sign is a horā; there, among odd signs, the first is of the Sun and the second of the Moon; in even signs, [the first] is of the Moon and the second of the Sun. In all signs, there are three decans; these [belong to] the lords of the first, fifth, and ninth signs.
Of the signs facing east, the navāṃśakas begin with the Ram; of those facing south, they begin with the Makara; of those facing west, they begin with the Scales; of those facing north, they begin with the Crab. The very first navāṃśaka of all is vargottama. The final degrees of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are gaṇḍāntas.
In sign after sign, there are twelve twelfth-parts, [each assigned] by pairs [of signs].
The thirty-degree divisions [triṃśāṃśakas]: five are of Mars, then five of Saturn, then eight of Jupiter, seven of Mercury, and eight of Venus in an odd sign; but in an even sign, eight are of Venus, then seven of Mercury, then eight of Jupiter, five of Saturn, and five of Mars.
Thus the ascendant has six factors. Conjoined with or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter, Mercury, or Venus, it becomes strong.
Free from them and aspected by the rest, it would be weak in strength.
And thus a planet situated in the seventh [house] aspects a sign with full aspect.
Those situated in the fourth and eighth should be known as [aspecting] with a quarter aspect, and in the fifth and ninth with a half aspect.
And in the third and tenth with a quarter aspect; situated in the first, second, eighth, and twelfth, it does not aspect.

तत्रस्थं गृहमध्येर्लग्नमुदयं विलग्नकेन्द्रं त्रिकोणम्।
शरीरमिति लग्नस्याख्या, धान्यकुटुम्बं च द्वितीयस्य, उपचयं योधभ्रातृदुश्चिक्याख्यं तृतीयस्य, मित्रगृहं हिबुकं सुखवाहनकेन्द्रपालकाख्याश्चतुर्थस्य, पुत्रत्रिकोणबुद्धिसंज्ञाः पञ्चमस्य, उपचयारिसंज्ञे षष्ठस्य, जायाजामित्रास्तमार्गश्च्यवनद्यूनसंज्ञाः सप्तमस्म, छिद्रायुसंज्ञे चाष्टस्य, धर्मत्रिकोणत्रित्रिकोणच्छिद्रसंज्ञा नवमस्य, कर्मकेन्द्राकाशमेषूरणोपचयाख्यापनया दशमस्य, उपचयायलाभद्रव्याख्या एकादशस्य, रिष्फ ऽद्यून' सव्ययाख्या द्वादशस्येति ॥
सर्वेभ्यः केन्द्रसंज्ञेभ्यो द्वितीयः पणफरः सर्वस्मात्पणफरात् द्वितीय आपो क्लिम इति ॥
आदित्याक्रान्तराशेः द्वितीयो वेशि, द्वादशे बोसि, उभये उभयचरी चन्द्रात् द्वितीयः सुनफा ।
द्वादशश्चानफा ।
उभयोरपि लग्नश्च स्वामिनदुरुधरासंज्ञासमेतौ अत्र सहस्ररश्मिरादित्यः नात्युच्चो न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलः पैत्तिकोऽस्थिसारो रक्तंश्यामः पापः पुरुषः क्षत्रियः कालात्मा राजा प्राग्द्वारो दक्षिणस्यां वा दिशि उदगयने कृष्णपक्षे च बली 5॥ चन्द्रमाः सहस्ररश्मिः तत्र वर्तुलाङ्गः दर्शनीयः स्वक्षः कफवातात्मा रुधिरसारः गौरः क्षीणः पापः पूर्णः सौम्यः स्त्रीग्रहः वैश्यः कालशमनः राजा पूर्वोत्तराभिमुखः उत्तरस्यां दिशि रात्रावुदगयने शुक्लपक्षे च बलवानिति ॥
2.34.m:
Situated therein, the ascendant [or] rising sign is in the middle of the house; it is a center and a trine.
"Body" is the name of the ascendant; "grain" and "family" of the second; "growth," "warrior," "brother," and "duścikya" are the names of the third; "friend's house," "hibuka," "happiness," "vehicle," and "guardian of the center" are the names of the fourth; "son," "trine," and "intellect" are designations of the fifth; "growth" and "enemy" are designations of the sixth; "wife," "jāmitra," "setting," "path," "fall," and "dyūna" are designations of the seventh; "vulnerability" and "longevity" are designations of the eighth; "dharma," "trine," "third trine," and "vulnerability" are designations of the ninth; "action," "center," "sky," "meṣūraṇa," "growth," and "apānaya" are names of the tenth; "growth," "income," "gain," and "wealth" are names of the eleventh; and "riṣpha," "dyūna," and "expenditure" are names of the twelfth.

The second from all those designated as centers is the succedent; the second from every succedent is the cadent.
The second from the sign occupied by the sun is veśi, the twelfth is vosi, and if both [are occupied], it is ubhayacarī. The second from the moon is sunaphā,
the twelfth is anaphā,
and if both [are occupied], it is durudharā, along with the lord of the ascendant. Here, the sun possesses a thousand rays; he is not very tall, has the circular girth of a banyan tree, is bilious, has bone as his essence, is dark-red, is a malefic, is male, is a kṣatriya, is the soul of Time, is a king, has an eastern gate, or is strong in the southern direction, during the northward course of the sun, and in the dark fortnight. The moon has a thousand rays; therein he has rounded limbs, is handsome, has fine eyes, is of phlegmatic and windy nature, has blood as his essence, is fair, is a malefic when waning and a benefic when full, is a female planet, is a vaiśya, is the pacifier of Time, is a king, faces northeast, and is strong in the northern direction, at night, during the northward course of the sun, and in the bright fortnight.

2.34.d:
भौमो नवरश्मिः ह्रस्वः पिङ्गाक्षः कपिलः पैत्तिको मजासारो रक्तगौरः पापः पुरुषग्रहः क्षत्रियः कालस्य सत्त्वं सेनानीः दक्षिणाभिमुखो वक्रे दक्षिणस्यां दिशि कृष्णपक्षे रात्रौ च बलवानिति ॥
बुधोष्टरश्मिर्मध्यमरूपः प्रमाणप्रकृतिः त्वक्सारः दूर्वाश्यामः सौम्यो न्यग्रोधसमेतप्रकृतिर्भवति नपुंसकः शूद्रः कालस्य वाक् युवराजः उदङ्मुखः उत्तरस्यां दिशि सर्वकालं वक्रे शुक्लपक्षे च बलवानिति ॥
सौरः सप्तरश्मिः कृष्णो दीर्घः वातप्रकृतिः पापो नपुंसकः कालस्य दुःखः प्रेष्यः पार्थिवाभिमुखः तस्यामेव दिशि रात्रौ वक्रे शुक्लपक्षे च बलवानिति॥
सर्वे च ग्रहाः स्वसंवत्सरे स्वायने स्वर्तौ स्वमासे स्वपक्षे स्वदिने स्वहोरायां स्ववर्गे बलवन्तो भवन्ति वर्गोत्तमस्थ स्वोच्चस्थः स्वत्रिकोणस्थश्च ग्रहयुद्धे च जयी रश्मिवपुर्धरश्च बलवान्भवति।
आदित्यस्य चन्द्राङ्गारकजीवा मित्राणि बुधस्समः शुक्रसौरावरीः॥
चन्द्रस्य सूर्यबुधौ मित्रे शेषाः समाः॥
भौमस्य जीवेन्दूष्णकराः सुहृदः, ज्ञोरिः सितार्कजौ समौ॥
बुधस्य सूर्यसितौ मित्रे, हिमगुः शत्रुः, भौमजीवशनैःश्चराः समाः ॥
जीवस्य सूर्येन्दुभौमा मित्राणि, रविसुतो मध्यः, सौम्यसितावरी ॥
शुक्रस्य बुधसौरौ मित्रे भौमजीवौ मध्यस्थौ सूर्येन्दू अरी ॥।
सौरस्य बुधशुक्रौ मित्रे जीवो मध्यस्थः आदित्येन्दुकुजा रिपवः ॥
तत्काले च ग्रहाद्ग्रहो द्वितीयतृतीयतामेति मध्यश्चारितामरिरमित्रताम् ॥
तत्र गर्भः प्रथममासि कललं भवति द्वितीये घनीभवति ॥
2.34.m:
Mars has nine rays, is short, has reddish-brown eyes, is tawny, is bilious, has marrow as his essence, is reddish-fair, is a malefic, is a male planet, is a kṣatriya, is the courage of Time, is a commander of an army, faces south, is retrograde, and is strong in the southern direction, in the dark fortnight, and at night.
Mercury has eight rays, is of medium form, has standard constitution, has skin as his essence, is dark as dūrvā grass, is a benefic, has a constitution resembling a banyan tree, is a neuter, is a śūdra, is the speech of Time, is a crown prince, faces north, and is strong in the northern direction, at all times, when retrograde, and in the bright fortnight.
Saturn has seven rays, is black, is tall, is of windy constitution, is a malefic, is a neuter, is the grief of Time, is a servant, faces the earth, and is strong in that same direction, at night, when retrograde, and in the bright fortnight.
And all planets are strong in their own year, their own solstice, their own season, their own month, their own fortnight, their own day, their own planetary hour, and their own division. A planet situated in the highest division, in its own exaltation, in its own trine, victorious in planetary war, and endowed with radiant rays becomes strong.
The moon, Mars, and Jupiter are friends of the sun; Mercury is neutral; Venus and Saturn are enemies.
The sun and Mercury are friends of the moon; the rest are neutral.
Jupiter, the moon, and the sun are friends of Mars; Mercury is an enemy; Venus and Saturn are neutral.
The sun and Venus are friends of Mercury; the cold-rayed [moon] is an enemy; Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn are neutral.
The sun, the moon, and Mars are friends of Jupiter; the son of the sun [Saturn] is neutral; Mercury and Venus are enemies.
Mercury and Saturn are friends of Venus; Mars and Jupiter are neutral; the sun and the moon are enemies.
Mercury and Venus are friends of Saturn; Jupiter is neutral; the sun, the moon, and Mars are enemies.
And at that time, a planet stands in a second or third [relation] from a planet: it enters a neutral, enemy, or friendly state according to its movement.
Therein, in the first month, the embryo is an unformed mass; in the second, it solidifies;

tṛtīye'vayavāścāsya bhavanti caturthe'sthīni pañcame tvak ṣaṣṭhe balaṃ saptame lomāni aṣṭame kṣudra naṣame udvegaḥ daśame prasavaḥ tatrāsya māsakrameṇa śukrāṅgārakabṛhaspatidivākaracandrasaurabudhā vā ..
lagnādhipaticandrārkāḥ patayaḥ ādhānakāle yaḥ kaluṣo bhavati sa svamāse garbhapīḍāṃ karoti yo'nyagrahavijitaḥ ketūlkābhihataḥ sa svamāse garbhapātāya bhavati janmalagna pañcamaṣaṣṭhasaptamāṣṭamanavameṣu candramāḥ pāpayuta. saumyadṛgyogavarjito vā tasya maraṇāya bhavati lagnacaturthasaptamāṣṭameṣu pāpadvayamadhyagataśca ṣaṣṭhāṣṭamayoḥ pāpadṛṣṭo'pi ṣaṣṭhāṣṭamairanyatame budhajīvaśukrāṇāmanyatamo vakriṇā pāpena dṛṣṭaḥ saumyagraheṇa cādṛṣṭo maraṇāya lagnapaścānte pāpayutaśca yatra tatra rāśau navamoṃśaḥ pāpasandhyāyāṃ candrahorā ca catvāryapi ca kendrāṇi yamārkacandrabhaumasaurāvetare bhacakra pūrvārdhe pāpāḥ paścārdhe saumyāḥ karkaṭavṛścikānyatamodaye ca kendrāṣṭameneti .

evamariṣṭānyaṣṭavarṣāntare vidyāt .
atha tātkālikasya grahasya rāśibhāgaliptā aṣṭādhikaśatārddhagaṇanā kāryā bhagaṇānāṃ dvādaśāvaśeṣe varpamāsadinaghaṭikā bhavanti .
2.34.d:
तृतीयेऽवयवाश्चास्य भवन्ति चतुर्थेऽस्थीनि पञ्चमे त्वक् षष्ठे बलं सप्तमे लोमानि अष्टमे क्षुद्र नषमे उद्वेगः दशमे प्रसवः तत्रास्य मासक्रमेण शुक्राङ्गारकबृहस्पतिदिवाकरचन्द्रसौरबुधा वा ॥
लग्नाधिपतिचन्द्रार्काः पतयः आधानकाले यः कलुषो भवति स स्वमासे गर्भपीडां करोति योऽन्यग्रहविजितः केतूल्काभिहतः स स्वमासे गर्भपाताय भवति जन्मलग्न पञ्चमषष्ठसप्तमाष्टमनवमेषु चन्द्रमाः पापयुत। सौम्यदृग्योगवर्जितो वा तस्य मरणाय भवति लग्नचतुर्थसप्तमाष्टमेषु पापद्वयमध्यगतश्च षष्ठाष्टमयोः पापदृष्टोऽपि षष्ठाष्टमैरन्यतमे बुधजीवशुक्राणामन्यतमो वक्रिणा पापेन दृष्टः सौम्यग्रहेण चादृष्टो मरणाय लग्नपश्चान्ते पापयुतश्च यत्र तत्र राशौ नवमोंशः पापसन्ध्यायां चन्द्रहोरा च चत्वार्यपि च केन्द्राणि यमार्कचन्द्रभौमसौरावेतरे भचक्र पूर्वार्धे पापाः पश्चार्धे सौम्याः कर्कटवृश्चिकान्यतमोदये च केन्द्राष्टमेनेति ।
पापैः क्षीणचन्द्रोदये च लग्नान्यधर्माष्टमस्थैः चन्द्रशनैश्चरार्कभौमैः जीवे च बलहीने चन्द्रग्रहेण कालः सक्रूरे चन्द्रे लग्नगे भौमेष्टमे मात्रा सह म्रियते ऐवंविधेर्के शस्त्रेण ।
एवमरिष्टान्यष्टवर्षान्तरे विद्यात् ।
अथ तात्कालिकस्य ग्रहस्य राशिभागलिप्ता अष्टाधिकशतार्द्धगणना कार्या भगणानां द्वादशावशेषे वर्पमासदिनघटिका भवन्ति ।
2.34.m:
in the third, its limbs develop; in the fourth, its bones; in the fifth, its skin; in the sixth, its strength; in the seventh, its body hair; in the eighth, its minor parts; in the ninth, its agitation; and in the tenth, its delivery. There, in the order of its months, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, the sun, the moon, Saturn, and Mercury—
or the lord of the ascendant, the moon, and the sun—are the rulers. Whichever [planet] is afflicted at the time of conception causes distress to the fetus in its own month; whichever is conquered by another planet or struck by a comet or meteor causes miscarriage of the fetus in its own month. If the moon is in the natal ascendant, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, or ninth house joined by a malefic, or deprived of the aspect or conjunction of a benefic, it leads to the child's death. If [the moon] is in the ascendant, fourth, seventh, or eighth, situated between two malefics, or even if it is in the sixth or eighth aspected by a malefic; or if any one of Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, situated in either the sixth or eighth, is aspected by a retrograde malefic and not aspected by a benefic planet, it leads to death. If there is a malefic joined at the end of the western ascendant, or in whatever sign the ninth navāṃśa is [occupied by a malefic] at an inauspicious twilight and in a lunar horā; or if all four centers—Yama, the sun, the moon, Mars, and Saturn, or others—contain malefics in the eastern half of the zodiacal wheel and benefics in the western half, and with either Cancer or Scorpio rising, and [malefics] in the centers or the eighth [house];
and if at the rising of a waning moon [aspected] by malefics, or when the moon, Saturn, the sun, and Mars are situated in houses other than the ascendant, ninth, and eighth, and Jupiter is devoid of strength, death is caused by a lunar eclipse. When the moon is in the ascendant with a malefic and Mars is in the eighth, he dies together with his mother; when the sun is situated in such a manner, [he dies] by a weapon.
Thus one should recognize fatal afflictions occurring within eight years.
Now, the signs, degrees, and minutes of the planet at that time should be calculated by multiplying by one hundred and eight and dividing in half; when twelve remain from the revolutions, they become the years, months, days, and ghaṭikās.

2.34.d:
लग्नाद्द्वादशस्थः सर्वमपहरति एकादशगो अर्द्धम् दशमस्थस्त्र्यांशं नवमस्थश्च चतुर्थमष्टमस्थः पञ्चमम् । सप्तमस्थः षष्ठमेवं पापः सौम्यस्तदर्द्धं बहुष्वेकर्क्षगेषु बल वानेवैकोङ्गारकवर्जं शत्रुक्षेत्रस्थस्त्र्यांशं हरति शुक्रसौरवर्जितावस्तमिताश्च सर्वेश्वरीमवेधम् ।
वर्गोत्तमस्वराशिद्रेष्काणांशगतश्च द्विगुणं हानिवृद्धी वा ।
एकामेव महतीं प्रयच्छति एवं निर्णीतमायुर्यावद्येन ग्रहेण दत्तं तावत्कालं दंशा ज्ञेया लग्राद्दशा च ग्रहवद्बलवांश्च लग्नो भक्तराशितुल्यानि ,वर्षाण्यन्यानि प्रयच्छति ।
दशा च लग्नार्कचन्द्राणां बलवतः प्रथमा भवति ततस्तत्कण्टकस्थानां बलवत्क्रमेणैव ततः पणफरगतानां तत आपो क्लिमगतानामिति ।
तत्रोच्चत्रिकोणस्वक्षेत्रवर्गोत्तमगतस्य शुभा विपरीतस्य चाशुभा लग्नदशा लग्नपग्रहवशेनागतस्यैकराशिगोग्रहोवमाननिदस्यस्व गुणानसापतिनवमपञ्चमगस्तृतीयेन चतुर्थगश्चतुर्थेन सप्तमगः सप्तमगेन बहुष्वेकोऽवयवो अथान्त्यदशायामष्टमग्रहवशेन म्रियते तत्रार्केणाग्निना, चन्द्रमसा सलिलेन, भौमेन शस्त्रेण, बुधेन ज्वरेण, जीवेनामयेन, शुक्रेण तृष्णया, सौरेण क्षुधा, अष्टमं ग्रहरहितं यो ग्रहो बलवान्पश्यति
तद्धातुकायेन म्रियते अष्टमे ग्रहयोगदृग्रहिते द्वाविंशः द्रेष्काणाधिपतिकथितमृत्युना म्रियते ।
2.34.m:
[A planet] situated in the twelfth from the ascendant takes away all [longevity]; positioned in the eleventh, half; situated in the tenth, a third; situated in the ninth, a fourth; situated in the eighth, a fifth; situated in the seventh, a sixth. A malefic [does this]; a benefic, half of that. When many [planets] are in one sign, only the strongest one [reduces longevity], except Mars. Situated in an enemy's sign, it takes away a third; and combustion [reduces] everything, except for Venus and Saturn.
And when placed in Vargottama, its own sign, decanate, or navāṃśa, [there is] doubling, or loss and gain [respectively].
[When several apply,] it yields only one greatest [reduction or addition]. In this way longevity is determined. For as long a time as was given by a planet, that period should be known as its daśā. And from the ascendant, the daśā [is reckoned] like a planet; and a strong ascendant gives other years equal to the divided sign.
And the first daśā belongs to the strongest among the ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon; then to those situated in angles, in order of strength; then to those situated in succedent houses (paṇaphara); then to those situated in cadent houses (āpoklima).
Therein, [the period] of one situated in its exaltation, trine, own sign, or Vargottama is auspicious; of the opposite, inauspicious. In the ascendant-daśā, according to the ruling planet of the ascendant, a planet that has entered into a single sign … [regarding] the ninth, fifth, third, fourth, or seventh, when many are present, one [part governs]. Now, in the final daśā, one dies under the influence of the planet in the eighth house: therein by the Sun, through fire; by the Moon, through water; by Mars, through a weapon; by Mercury, through fever; by Jupiter, through disease; by Venus, through thirst; by Saturn, through hunger. Whichever strong planet aspects the eighth devoid of planets,
[the native] dies through the bodily humor [governed by] it. If the eighth is devoid of any conjunction or aspect of a planet, one dies through the death declared by the lord of the twenty-second decanate.

2.34.d:
शुक्राद्द्विपञ्चषण्णवदशैकादशेषु सौरात्त्रिपञ्चसप्तदशैकादशेषु लग्नात्प्रथमद्विचतुःपञ्चषट्सप्तदशैकादशेषु जीवात्पञ्चाष्टनवमैकादशेषु स्वात्प्रथमद्विचतुःपंचाष्टनवमैकादशेषु सौरात्त्रिचतुःपञ्चाष्टनवमैकादशेषु लग्नात्प्रथम द्वित्रिचतुःपञ्चाष्टनवमैकादशेषु सौरोऽर्कात्प्रथमद्विचतुःसप्ताष्टदशमैकादशेषु चन्द्राद्द्विषडेकादशेषु भौमात्त्रिपञ्चषड्दशैकादशेषु बुधात्षष्ठनवदशैकादश द्वादशेषु जीवात्पञ्चषष्ठैकादशद्वादशेषु शुक्रात्षडेकादशद्वादशेषु स्वात्त्रिपञ्चषडेकादशेषु लग्नात्प्रथमद्विचतुर्दशमेषु येषु नोक्तः शुभस्तेषु सर्व एवाशुभो भवति ।
शुभाशुभविशेषश्च चारवशात्फलं प्रयच्छति दशाफलमव्यभिचारि अष्टवर्गफलमशुभं शान्त्यादिभिरुपहतं भवति चात्र-अनफासु नफास्थाने न शस्ते ग्रहवर्जिते ॥
सर्वेषां चैव केन्द्राणां शून्यता न प्रशस्यते ॥
कर्किणी च झषाणां च चरमोंऽशस्तथैव च ॥
शत्रुक्षेत्रस्तथा नीचो ग्रहाणां गर्हणा स्थितिः ॥
सूर्यमण्डलगाश्चैव न प्रशस्तास्तथा ग्रहाः ॥
जन्मपो लग्नपश्चैव श्रेष्ठौ बलसमन्वितौ ॥
तावेतौ विबलौ यस्य तमधन्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
एकोऽपि परमोच्चस्थो मित्रदृष्टस्तथा ग्रहः ॥
जनयत्यवनीशत्वं शत्रुपक्षक्षयङ्करम् ॥
अतीव स्वस्थो विज्ञेयः स्वोच्चे लग्नगते ग्रहः ॥
भावमानं न प्रशस्तं तथा जन्मनि कीर्तितम् ॥
चन्द्रः शस्तो हि विज्ञेयो दृष्टे क्षेत्राधिपेन तु ॥
तं मित्रेण तथा ब्रह्मन् प्रशस्तं तदरातिभिः ॥
चत्वारोऽपि यदा केन्द्रा युक्ताः स्वोच्चगतैर्ग्रहैः ॥
तदा जातो विनिर्दिष्टः समस्तवसुधाधिपः ॥
त्रयो वा तस्य यस्य स्युर्वशे पृथ्वी ससागरा ॥
2.34.m:
from Venus, in the second, fifth, sixth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh; from Saturn, in the third, fifth, seventh, tenth, and eleventh; from the ascendant, in the first, second, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, tenth, and eleventh; [Venus] from Jupiter, in the fifth, eighth, ninth, and eleventh; from its own, in the first, second, fourth, fifth, eighth, ninth, and eleventh; from Saturn, in the third, fourth, fifth, eighth, ninth, and eleventh; from the ascendant, in the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, eighth, ninth, and eleventh. Saturn [is auspicious] from the Sun in the first, second, fourth, seventh, eighth, tenth, and eleventh; from the Moon, in the second, sixth, and eleventh; from Mars, in the third, fifth, sixth, tenth, and eleventh; from Mercury, in the sixth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth; from Jupiter, in the fifth, sixth, eleventh, and twelfth; from Venus, in the sixth, eleventh, and twelfth; from its own, in the third, fifth, sixth, and eleventh; from the ascendant, in the first, second, fourth, and tenth. In those [places] where it is not stated as auspicious, in all of them it is inauspicious.
And the distinction of auspicious and inauspicious yields fruit through transits. The fruit of the daśā is unfailing; the inauspicious fruit of the aṣṭakavarga is countered by pacifications and the like. And in this regard: / When the places of anaphā and sunaphā are devoid of planets, it is not praised; / and the emptiness of all the angles is certainly not praised. / The last portion of Cancer and of Pisces, / as well as situated in an enemy's sign or debilitated, is a blameworthy position for planets. / And planets situated in the solar orb are likewise not praised. / The lord of the birth[-star] and the lord of the ascendant, endowed with strength, are both excellent; / one whose two [lords] are devoid of strength should be designated unfortunate. / Even a single planet situated in its highest exaltation and aspected by a friend / produces kingship that destroys the enemy's side. / A planet situated in its own exaltation in the ascendant should be known as exceedingly well situated; / the measure of bhāva is said not to be praised in such a birth. / The Moon is certainly known to be auspicious when aspected by the lord of its sign, / and so too by a friend, O brahmin; [it is] praised [when aspected] by its enemies [only under specific conditions]. / When all four angles are occupied by planets situated in their exaltations, / then the one born is proclaimed a ruler of the entire earth; / or he who has three [so placed] has the earth along with the oceans under his sway.

2.34.d:
द्वौ तु केन्द्रगतौ यस्य ग्रहौ कर्किणि चन्द्रमाः ॥
सोऽपि राजा विनिर्दिष्ट एकेनापि तथा द्विज ॥
सर्वैस्तु परमोच्चस्थैस्त्रैलोक्याधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥
मित्रक्षेत्रे तथात्मीये तथा वर्गोत्तमेष्वपि ॥
स्वोच्चे वा स्वत्रिकोणे वा ग्रहाणां शस्यते स्थितिः ॥
ग्रहाणां चतुरादीनां तथा योगो विगर्हितः ॥
राजवंशे तथा भूपास्त्र्याद्यैः स्वस्वग्रहोपगैः ॥
अन्यवंशभवा भूपाः पञ्चाढ्यैरपि च द्विज ॥
त्रिकोणोच्चगतैरेव विशेषेण द्विजोत्तम ॥
भावे विकारकाः सौम्याः पापा भावविनाशनाः ॥
तृतीये च तथा षष्ठे दशमैकादशेऽपि च ॥
स्थितिः पापग्रहाणां च प्रशस्ता परिकीर्तिता ॥
षष्ठाः सर्वग्रहाः शस्ता न शस्ता द्वादशाष्टमाः ॥
चन्द्रे लग्नगते मूर्खा विना वृषकुलीरके ॥
सूर्ये लग्नगते ज्ञेयास्तथा जयबलाननाः ॥
बलवद्ग्रहयुक्तैश्च विज्ञेया ईश(रूप)चेष्टितैः ॥
चन्द्रद्युग्रा (पुष्पा) विशीलाश्च विज्ञातव्यास्तथैव च॥
पापाः पापबला ज्ञेयाः सौम्याः सौम्यबलास्तथा॥।
चन्द्रादुपचयर्क्षस्थैर्ग्रहा ज्ञेया धनान्विताः ॥
एतावदुक्तं सारं ते होरासंग्रहमुत्तमम् ॥
2.34.m:
One who has two planets positioned in the angles and the Moon in Cancer,
he too is declared a king, and likewise even by one, O twice-born.
With all planets in their highest exaltation, one would become the lord of the three worlds.
In a friendly sign, in one's own sign, and also in navāṃśas identical to their signs,
in one's own exaltation, or in one's own trine, the position of planets is praised.
A conjunction of four or more planets is condemned.
Kings in a royal lineage are produced by three or more planets situated in their own places,
and kings born in other lineages are produced by five or more, O twice-born,
especially when situated in trines and exaltations, O foremost of the twice-born.
Benefics modify the houses; malefics destroy the houses.
And in the third, sixth, tenth, and eleventh houses,
the position of malefic planets is proclaimed praiseworthy.
All planets in the sixth house are praiseworthy; those in the twelfth and eighth are not.
With the Moon in the ascendant, men are fools, except in Taurus and Cancer.
With the Sun in the ascendant, they should be known as having faces endowed with victory and power.
By planets endowed with strength, they should be known as acting like lords.
[By inauspicious planets], they should be known as fierce and devoid of good conduct.
Malefics are known to have malefic power; benefics likewise to have benefic power.
By planets situated in signs of growth from the Moon, they should be known as endowed with wealth.
Thus far have I told you the excellent essence, a summary of Horā.

अथ भगवन्तं भुवनोत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहारकारकं चराचरगुरुमतियशसमभिगम्य भृगुर्विज्ञापयामास ।
भगवञ्ज्योतिःशास्त्रं विना गणितेन दुःखगाहमतो गौणेतविधिमाचक्ष्व ।
तमुवाच श्रीभगवाञ्छृणु वत्स गणितज्ञानम् ।
अनादिनिधनः कालः प्रजापतिर्विष्णुस्तस्य ग्रहगत्यनुसारेण ज्ञानं गणितम् ।
तत्रार्कभागभोगः सौराहोरात्रास्तिथिश्च चान्द्रः अर्कोदयात्तदुदयात्सावनः ।
चन्द्रनक्षत्रभोगो नक्षत्रम् ।
सावनोऽहोरात्रा नराणाम् ।
तेषामार्कं दिनं त्र्यर्का रात्रिः चन्द्रमसः पितॄणामहोरात्रम् ।
तेषां कृष्णाष्टम्यामर्कोदयः ।
अमावस्यायां मध्याह्नः ।
शुक्लाष्टम्यामर्कास्तमयः ।
पौर्णमास्यामर्धरात्रम् ।
अर्कभगणभोगो दिव्योऽहोरात्रः ।
तेषामर्कस्य मेषप्रवेशे सूर्योदयः, कर्कटप्रवेशे मध्याह्नः ।
तुलाप्रवेथेऽस्तमयः मकरप्रवेशेर्धरात्रः ॥
मेषादिस्थे मध्यमे जीवे जीवमानैराश्वयुजादयो वत्सरा भवन्ति ।
लङ्कायामर्कोदये चैत्रशुक्लप्रतिपदारम्भेऽर्कदिनादावश्विन्यादौ किंस्तुघ्नादौ रात्रावथार्कोदये काले प्रवृत्तिः।
होरादिप्रवृत्तिश्च ।
लङ्कातश्च यावन्मेरोर्याम्योत्तरदेशान्तरे रेखा तत्पूर्वेणापरेण बलकालार्कोदयकालप्रवृत्तिः लङ्कार्योदयकालं तन्मण्डलम् ।
स्वदेशविषुवादर्कोदयविषुवन्मण्डलत्वं प्रतिदिनं चरदलवशेनार्कोदयः ।
क्षितिजं मण्डलम् ।
तत्रार्कभगणभोगेन सौराब्दः ।
येषामब्दानां वै त्रयेण गुणमेकं वेदः कलियुगम्, द्विगुणं द्वापरम्, त्रिगुणं त्रेता, चतुर्गुणं कृतम् शून्यचतुष्टयं यमाग्निवेगाश्चतुर्युगम् ।
एकसप्ततिश्चतुर्युगानि मन्वन्तरम् ।
चतुर्दश मन्वन्तराणि कल्पः ।
2.34.m:
2.168
Puṣkara said:
Then Bhṛgu, having approached the Blessed One, the maker of the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the world, the teacher of the moving and unmoving, possessing immense fame, made a request:
'Blessed Lord, astronomy is difficult to fathom without calculation; therefore explain the system of mathematics.'
To him the Blessed Lord said: 'Listen, my child, to the knowledge of calculation.
Time is without beginning and without end; it is Prajāpati Viṣṇu; knowledge of it according to the motions of planets is calculation.
There, the passage through a degree of the Sun is a solar day-and-night; a lunar day is lunar; a civil [day] is from one sunrise of the Sun to the next sunrise.
The Moon's passage through a lunar mansion is a sidereal [day].
A civil day-and-night belongs to mortals.
A solar day is their day; the three solar [units] make the night; a day-and-night of the ancestors belongs to the Moon.
For them, sunrise is on the eighth day of the dark fortnight;
noon is at the new moon;
sunset is on the eighth day of the bright fortnight;
midnight is at the full moon.
A revolution of the Sun through the zodiac is a celestial day-and-night.
For them, sunrise is upon the Sun's entry into Aries; midday upon entry into Cancer;
sunset upon entry into Libra; midnight upon entry into Capricorn.
When the mean Jupiter is at the beginning of Aries, years such as Āśvayuja occur according to Jupiter's measures.
At sunrise in Laṅkā, at the beginning of the first day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, at the beginning of Sunday, at the beginning of Aśvinī, at the beginning of the Kiṃstughna [karaṇa], at night or at sunrise, the commencement of time occurs,
and the commencement of the horā and so forth.
And along the meridian between Laṅkā and Meru, to its east and west, is the commencement of time measured by power and sunrise; that circle is the time of sunrise at Laṅkā.
From the equinox of one's own locality, the equinoctial circle of sunrise [is determined]; each day sunrise occurs by virtue of the ascensional difference.
The horizon is the circle.
There, a solar year is [completed] by a revolution of the Sun through the zodiac.
One [cycle] multiplied by three of those years is the Veda [four]; Kali age; twice that is Dvāpara; three times that is Tretā; four times that is Kṛta; four zeros, twins [2], fires [3], speed [4] [4,320,000] is the four ages.
Seventy-one four ages make a Manvantara.
Fourteen Manvantaras make an aeon.

2.34.d:

शुक्रमन्दस्य गुणशरवसवः ।
सौरमन्दस्य शशिवेदाः ॥
चन्द्रपातस्य वसुरसशशिरुद्राग्निदशनयमलाः ।

यस्याल्पाः कक्षा वर्गदशभागमूलकक्षा कर्णस्तदर्धेनोपरिभवो ग्रहावस्थानं कर्णवर्गस्य दशगुणितस्य मूलकक्षा ।
2.34.m:
And at the beginning and in the intervals of the Manvantaras, the dawn is of the measure of the Kṛta age.
Thus an aeon consists of the four ages.
In an aeon, seven zeros, the Vasus [8], fires [3], and Vedas [4] [4,320,000,000] are the revolutions of the Sun.
Five zeros, qualities [3], fires [3], five [5], seven [7], senses [5], Moon [1] [57,753,300,000] are those of the Moon.
Of Mars, the second, five, eight, nine, eight, nine, two, twin pair [2,296,898,522].
Of Mercury, eight, nine, eight, nine, nine, Rāmas [3], fires [3], nine, same, Moon [1,793,399,898].
Of Jupiter, five, five, two, six, five, two, six, eyes [2], two, acts [4], flavors [6], qualities [3] [364,226,526,255].
Of Venus, twins [2], nine, Aśvins [2], nine, eight, fires [3], twins [2], void [0], mountains [7] [7,023,892,922].
Of Saturn, eight, nine, twins [2], mountains [7], flavors [6], five, Manus [14] [145,672,98].
The slow motion of the Sun has eight risings.
Of the Moon too, eight, senses [5], Vasus [8], senses [5], directions [10], eight, Vedas [4].
The slow [apogee] of Mars is twin, men [14], wings [2]; of the slow [apogee] of Mercury, two, three, qualities [3].
Of Jupiter, five, five, two, six, eyes [2], two, acts [4], flavors [6], qualities [3].
Of Venus, twins [2], nine, Aśvins [2], cows [9], eight, fires [3], twins [2], sky [0], mountains [7].
Of Saturn, eight, nine, twins [2], mountains [7], flavors [6], five, Manus [14].
The slow motion of the Sun is sky, eight risings.
Of the Moon too, eight, senses [5], Vasus [8], senses [5], directions [10], eight, Vedas [4].
The slow [apogee] of Mars is twin, men [14], wings [2].
Of the slow [apogee] of Mercury, two, three, qualities [3].
Of Jupiter's slow [apogee], arrows [5], arrows [5], Vasus [8].
Of Venus's slow [apogee], qualities [3], arrows [5], Vasus [8].
Of Saturn's slow [apogee], Moon [1], Vedas [4].
Of the Moon's node, Vasus [8], flavors [6], Moon [1], Rudras [11], fires [3], teeth [32], twins [2].
Of Mars's node, mountains [7], openings [9], twins [2].
Of Mercury's node, Moon [1], fires [3], senses [5], twins [2].
Of Jupiter's node, qualities [3], flavors [6].
Of Saturn's node, three, nine, Vasus [8].
Eight zeros, dissolution, flavors [6], sky [0], Sun [12], sages [7], Vasus [8], Moon [1].
Of the nine planets moving eastward, when divided by the fraction of the revolution of that whose aeon is being computed, the yojanas of its orbit are obtained.
That which has many revolutions has its orbit above; that which has few orbits has its orbit [below]. The orbit is the square root of one-tenth of the square [of the diameter]; the hypotenuse, and half of it, is the orbital position of the planet situated above; the base orbit is the square root of ten times the square of the hypotenuse.

2.34.d:
एवं सर्ववृत्तानां परिधिव्यासानयनम्।
यत्र च सर्वग्रहाणामेकत्वमेव दृश्यते सा खरसेन्दुयमकक्षा ।
तस्या योजनतलिप्ते मध्यमखखरसेन्दुयज्ञैर्यस्यैव कक्षा विभज्यन्ते तस्यैव लिप्तयोजनानि लभ्यन्ते । कल्पाद्ययोजनसमा वै कक्षाः ।
यदनन्तरं वितिमिरं रविः करोति पक्षपक्षेश्वतवोदार्कमण्डलप्रमाणम् ॥
वेदावेदाश्चन्द्रमसः ।

त्रयोदश बुधस्य ।

नव च शुक्रस्य ।
पञ्चदश सौरस्य ।
त्रिभागोनाश्चतुर्दशभागाः सूर्यस्य ।
एकत्रिंशद्भागाः षट्त्रिंशल्लिप्ताश्चन्द्रमसः ।
सप्ततिर्भौमस्य ।

त्रिंशच्छनैश्चरस्य ।
एवं परिधयो भौमस्य ।
शीघ्रपरिधिगुणवेराश्च संभागालिमाः चत्वारिंशद्बुधस्य ।
भागा यमाग्निचन्द्राः अष्टगुणा जीवस्य ।
वस्वर्थपक्षाः शुक्रस्य ॥
पञ्चविंशतिः सौरस्य ।
परिवेशेनोर्द्ध्वमधश्च ग्रहगतिर्ज्ञेया ।
खखरसेन्दुयमलानां षण्नवतिभागः प्रथमा ज्या ।
तदेवं प्रथमं ज्यान्तरा तस्य प्रथमजीवतया भागमुपहृत्याप्तं प्रथमज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य द्वितीयं ज्यान्तरं द्वितीयप्रथमज्यान्तरयोगे द्वितीयप्रथमं ज्यान्तरयोगो जीवा ।
ततः प्रथमं जीवाप्तं सद्वितीयज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य तृतीयं ज्यान्तरम् ।
ततः द्वितीयजीवयोगस्तृतीया ।
ततः प्रथमजीवात्संशोध्य चतुर्थं ज्यान्तरम् ॥
एवं तृतीयजीवायां दत्त्वा चतुर्थी ज्या ।
2.34.m:
Thus is the calculation of the circumference and diameter of all circles.
And where oneness of all planets is observed, that is the orbit of 21,600 [yojanas].
When its yojanas are converted to minutes, and the orbits of whichever planet are divided by the mean 21,600, that very planet's minutes and yojanas are obtained. Indeed, the orbits are equal to the yojanas from the beginning of the kalpa.
Next, the measure of the Sun's orb, which dispels darkness, in fortnight after fortnight, is [...].

15 for Mars,
60 for Mercury,
120 for Jupiter,
200 for Venus,
30 for Saturn.
The degrees of visibility and invisibility are 12 for the Moon,
17 for Mars,
13 for Mercury,
11 for Jupiter,
9 for Venus,
15 for Saturn.
[The diameters of the apogees are] 14 degrees less by a third for the Sun,
31 degrees and 36 minutes for the Moon,
70 for Mars,
38 for Mercury,
33 for Jupiter,
11 for Venus,
30 for Saturn.
Thus are the circumferences for Mars.
And the circumferences of the fast [epicycles]: 40 parts for Mercury,
132 degrees, multiplied by eight, for Jupiter,
258 for Venus,
25 for Saturn.
The planetary motion is to be known above and below from the halo.
The ninety-sixth part of 21,600 is the first sine.
Thus, that is the first sine-difference; dividing it by that first sine as divisor, and subtracting the quotient from the first sine-difference, [one obtains] the second sine-difference; when the second and first sine-differences are added together, the sum of the second and first sine-differences is the [second] sine.
Then, subtracting from that [sine-difference] the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine, [one obtains] the third sine-difference.
Then, the sum with the second sine is the third [sine].
Then, subtracting [the quotient] from the first sine, [one obtains] the fourth sine-difference.
Thus, adding it to the third sine gives the fourth sine.

2.34.s:
tasyāḥ prathamajīvāyāṃ bhāgamapahṛtyāptaṃ caturthājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya pañcamajyāntaram .
tataścaturthaṃ jīvāyāṃ dattvā ṣaṣṭhī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajīvāptaṃ pañcame jyāntaraṃ saṃśodhya ṣaṣṭhaṃ jyāntaraṃ pañcamajīvāyāṃ dattvā saptamī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajīvāptaṃ saptamajyāntarātsaṃśodhyāṣṭamam .
tatsaptamajīvāyāṃ dattvā navamī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajīvāntareṇāptaṃ daśamajyāntarātsaṃśodhya navamaṃ jyāntaram .
taṃ navamajīvāyāṃ dattvā daśamī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptama .
ekādaśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya dvādaśaṃ jyāntaram .
tadekādaśajīvāyāṃ dattvā dvādaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ dvādaśajyāntarātsaṃśodhya trayodaśaṃ jyāntaram .
tattrayodaśajīvāyāṃ dattvā caturdaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ caturdaśa jyāntarātsaṃśodhya pañcadaśajyāntaram .
tataścaturdaśajīvāyāṃ dattvā pañcadaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ pañcadaśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya ṣoḍaśaṃ jyāntaram .
tatpañcadaśajīvāyāṃ saṃśodhya ṣoḍaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ ṣoḍaśajyāntarātsaṃśodhya saptadaśaṃ jyāntaram .
tatṣoḍaśajīvāyāṃ dattvā saptadaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ saptadaśajyāntarātsaṃśodhyāṣṭādaśamaṃ jyāntaram ..
tatsaptadaśa jīvāyāṃ dattvāṣṭādaśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptam .
aṣṭādaśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya ekonaviṃśaṃ jyāntaram .
tadaṣṭādaśajīvāyāṃ dattvaikonaviṃśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptamekonaviṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya viṃśatitamaṃ jyāntaram .
tadekonaviṃśajīvāyāṃ dattvā viṃśatitamī jyā .
tataḥ prathama jyāvāptaṃ viṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhyaikaviṃśaṃ jyāntaram .
tadviṃśatijīvāyāṃ dattvā ekaviṃśī jyā.
2.34.d:
तस्याः प्रथमजीवायां भागमपहृत्याप्तं चतुर्थाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य पञ्चमज्यान्तरम् ।
ततश्चतुर्थं जीवायां दत्त्वा षष्ठी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमजीवाप्तं पञ्चमे ज्यान्तरं संशोध्य षष्ठं ज्यान्तरं पञ्चमजीवायां दत्त्वा सप्तमी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमजीवाप्तं सप्तमज्यान्तरात्संशोध्याष्टमम् ।
तत्सप्तमजीवायां दत्त्वा नवमी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमजीवान्तरेणाप्तं दशमज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य नवमं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तं नवमजीवायां दत्त्वा दशमी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तम ।
एकादशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य द्वादशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तदेकादशजीवायां दत्त्वा द्वादशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं द्वादशज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य त्रयोदशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तत्त्रयोदशजीवायां दत्त्वा चतुर्दशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं चतुर्दश ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य पञ्चदशज्यान्तरम् ।
ततश्चतुर्दशजीवायां दत्त्वा पञ्चदशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं पञ्चदशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य षोडशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तत्पञ्चदशजीवायां संशोध्य षोडशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं षोडशज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य सप्तदशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तत्षोडशजीवायां दत्त्वा सप्तदशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं सप्तदशज्यान्तरात्संशोध्याष्टादशमं ज्यान्तरम् ॥
तत्सप्तदश जीवायां दत्त्वाष्टादशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तम् ।
अष्टादशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य एकोनविंशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तदष्टादशजीवायां दत्त्वैकोनविंशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तमेकोनविंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य विंशतितमं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तदेकोनविंशजीवायां दत्त्वा विंशतितमी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथम ज्यावाप्तं विंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्यैकविंशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तद्विंशतिजीवायां दत्त्वा एकविंशी ज्या।
2.34.m:
Dividing it by that first sine, and subtracting the quotient from the fourth sine-difference, [one obtains] the fifth sine-difference.
Then, adding it to the fourth sine gives the sixth sine.
Then, subtracting from the fifth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the sixth sine-difference; adding it to the fifth sine gives the seventh sine.
Then, subtracting from the seventh sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the eighth [sine-difference].
Adding that to the seventh sine gives the ninth sine.
Then, subtracting from the tenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine-difference gives the ninth sine-difference.
Adding that to the ninth sine gives the tenth sine.
Then, the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine,
subtracted from the eleventh sine-difference, gives the twelfth sine-difference.
Adding that to the eleventh sine gives the twelfth sine.
Then, subtracting from the twelfth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the thirteenth sine-difference.
Adding that to the thirteenth sine gives the fourteenth sine.
Then, subtracting from the fourteenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the fifteenth sine-difference.
Then, adding it to the fourteenth sine gives the fifteenth sine.
Then, subtracting from the fifteenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the sixteenth sine-difference.
Subtracting [or adding] that to the fifteenth sine gives the sixteenth sine.
Then, subtracting from the sixteenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the seventeenth sine-difference.
Adding that to the sixteenth sine gives the seventeenth sine.
Then, subtracting from the seventeenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the eighteenth sine-difference.
Adding that to the seventeenth sine gives the eighteenth sine.
Then, the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine,
subtracted from the eighteenth [sine-difference], gives the nineteenth sine-difference.
Adding that to the eighteenth sine gives the nineteenth sine.
Then, subtracting from the nineteenth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twentieth sine-difference.
Adding that to the nineteenth sine gives the twentieth sine.
Then, subtracting from the twentieth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twenty-first sine-difference.
Adding that to the twentieth sine gives the twenty-first sine.

2.34.s:
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ ekaviṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya dvāviṃśaṃ jyāntaram .
tadekaviṃśajīvāyāṃ dattvā dvāviṃśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ dvāviṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya trayoviṃśaṃ jyāntaram ..
taddvāviṃśa jīvāyāṃ dattvā trayoviṃśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamaṃ jyāvāptaṃ trayoviṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya caturviṃśaṃ jyāntaram .
tattrayoviṃśajīvāyāṃ dattvā caturviṃśī jyā .
tataḥ prathamajyāvāptaṃ caturviṃśājjyāntarātsaṃśodhya pañcaṃviṃśaṃ jyāntaram .
taccaturviṃśajīvāyāṃ dattvā pañcaviṃśī jyā .
khakharasendukakṣāyāṃ ca vyāsāraṃ tadevānupadanyāsāyām .
jyāntavyastānāmantarālayoge caturviṃśatiḥ śarā bhavanti .
kramajyākṛtijīvābhistastatkramajyākṛtiḥ śare yāsāṃ liptānāṃ jīvā kriyate tatkendrastasya ca rāśitraye padākhyā prathamapadasthe tadgamaṃ caturthapadasthe cakrādūnam .
jyākendraliptā rāśiliptāṣṭavibhāgena vibhājyā .
labdhāṅgasamāśca sthāpyāḥ .
avaśeṣaṃ tadanantaraṃ jyāntareṇa guṇayet.
rāśiliptāṣṭabhāgena vibhajet.
labdhaṃ sthāpitajīvāyāṃ dattveṣṭa jyāsiddhiḥ .
kālakṣaṇebhyo liptatvena parikalpitebhyo jīvā kāryā .
liptābhyo yāvanti jyāntarāṇi saṃśuddhanti tāvanti saṃśodhyāvaśiṣṭabhāgaliptāṣṭabhāgāhatamaśuddhajyāntareṇa vibhajet. labdhahatāsu ādyaṣṭakabhāgaliptāsu kṣipet.
śarāntarairevaṃ śaracāpaḥ bhāgacaturviṃśatijyāparamāpakramajyā meṣādi stho viṣuvallekhāstho graho bhavati.
kulīrādisthaścāntareṇa .
paramāpakramāntastho bhavati.
tulādistho viṣuvallekhāsthaḥ makarādistho dakṣiṇena paramāpakramahatāṃ vyāsārdhena vibhajet.
labdhaṃ candrasphuṭavikṣepaḥ .
2.34.d:
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं एकविंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य द्वाविंशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तदेकविंशजीवायां दत्त्वा द्वाविंशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं द्वाविंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य त्रयोविंशं ज्यान्तरम् ॥
तद्द्वाविंश जीवायां दत्त्वा त्रयोविंशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमं ज्यावाप्तं त्रयोविंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य चतुर्विंशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तत्त्रयोविंशजीवायां दत्त्वा चतुर्विंशी ज्या ।
ततः प्रथमज्यावाप्तं चतुर्विंशाज्ज्यान्तरात्संशोध्य पञ्चंविंशं ज्यान्तरम् ।
तच्चतुर्विंशजीवायां दत्त्वा पञ्चविंशी ज्या ।
खखरसेन्दुकक्षायां च व्यासारं तदेवानुपदन्यासायाम् ।
ज्यान्तव्यस्तानामन्तरालयोगे चतुर्विंशतिः शरा भवन्ति ।
क्रमज्याकृतिजीवाभिस्तस्तत्क्रमज्याकृतिः शरे यासां लिप्तानां जीवा क्रियते तत्केन्द्रस्तस्य च राशित्रये पदाख्या प्रथमपदस्थे तद्गमं चतुर्थपदस्थे चक्रादूनम् ।
ज्याकेन्द्रलिप्ता राशिलिप्ताष्टविभागेन विभाज्या ।
लब्धाङ्गसमाश्च स्थाप्याः ।
अवशेषं तदनन्तरं ज्यान्तरेण गुणयेत्।
राशिलिप्ताष्टभागेन विभजेत्।
लब्धं स्थापितजीवायां दत्त्वेष्ट ज्यासिद्धिः ।
कालक्षणेभ्यो लिप्तत्वेन परिकल्पितेभ्यो जीवा कार्या ।
लिप्ताभ्यो यावन्ति ज्यान्तराणि संशुद्धन्ति तावन्ति संशोध्यावशिष्टभागलिप्ताष्टभागाहतमशुद्धज्यान्तरेण विभजेत्। लब्धहतासु आद्यष्टकभागलिप्तासु क्षिपेत्।
शरान्तरैरेवं शरचापः भागचतुर्विंशतिज्यापरमापक्रमज्या मेषादि स्थो विषुवल्लेखास्थो ग्रहो भवति।
कुलीरादिस्थश्चान्तरेण ।
परमापक्रमान्तस्थो भवति।
तुलादिस्थो विषुवल्लेखास्थः मकरादिस्थो दक्षिणेन परमापक्रमहतां व्यासार्धेन विभजेत्।
लब्धं चन्द्रस्फुटविक्षेपः ।
2.34.m:
Then, subtracting from the twenty-first sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twenty-second sine-difference.
Adding that to the twenty-first sine gives the twenty-second sine.
Then, subtracting from the twenty-second sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twenty-third sine-difference.
Adding that to the twenty-second sine gives the twenty-third sine.
Then, subtracting from the twenty-third sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twenty-fourth sine-difference.
Adding that to the twenty-third sine gives the twenty-fourth sine.
Then, subtracting from the twenty-fourth sine-difference the quotient obtained by dividing by the first sine gives the twenty-fifth sine-difference.
Adding that to the twenty-fourth sine gives the twenty-fifth sine.
And in the orbit of 21,600, the radius is just that in step-by-step arrangement.
By the sum of the intervals of the reversed sines, there are twenty-four versed sines.
From the sines produced by the regular sine order, there is that calculation of the regular sine; in the versed sine, the minutes for which the sine is made are its anomaly; and in three signs of that, it is called a quadrant; when situated in the first quadrant, it is its traversed portion; when situated in the fourth quadrant, it is subtracted from the circle.
The minutes of the anomaly of the sine should be divided by an eighth part of the minutes of a sign.
And [the parts] equal to the obtained unit should be set down.
One should multiply the remainder by the subsequent sine-difference,
[and] divide by the eighth part of the minutes of a sign.
Adding the quotient to the sine set down, the desired sine is accomplished.
The sine should be made from the time-moments assumed in minutes.
Subtracting from the minutes as many sine-differences as can be subtracted, one should divide [the remainder] multiplied by the eighth part of the remaining degrees and minutes by the unsubtracted sine-difference; one should add the quotient to the minutes of the initial eighth part.
In this way, from the versine-differences [comes] the arc of the versed sine; the sine of twenty-four degrees is the sine of greatest declination; situated at the beginning of Aries, a planet is on the celestial equator;
situated at the beginning of Cancer, it is at the distance,
it stands at the end of the greatest declination;
situated at the beginning of Libra, it is on the celestial equator; situated at the beginning of Capricorn, to the south; one should divide [the product of it] multiplied by the greatest declination by the radius:
the result obtained is the true latitude of the Moon.

2.34.s:
tātkālikaśīghraṃ sphuṭaṃ supāte yojyaṃ budhaśukrayoḥ svamadāvikṣepahatāṃ sphuṭāntyakarṇena vibhajeta. labdhaṃ tayoḥ sphuṭavikṣepaḥ .
tātkālikasphuṭagrahasphuṭapātayogajyāṃ bhaumajīvasaurāṇāṃ madhyavikṣepahatāṃ sphuṭāntyakarṇena vibhajet, labdhaṃ teṣāṃ sphuṭa vikṣepaḥ .
utkrānticāpasphuṭavikṣepayordiśaiko yogaḥ tajjīvasyakrāntiḥ, tasyā niyogaḥ śiṣyate sā dik tadgolasthaśca graho bhavati .
evaṃ grahāṇāmuttareṇa dakṣiṇena gatirjñeyā .
bhacakravaśenodayāstamayau kurvaṃtaḥ paścimena yānti .
pūrvāṃ vrajanto bhagaṇaparivartānkurvanti tatra ca sūryāśvapātaiḥ samameva laṅkādakṣiṇottararekhāyāḥ phālgunānte sarva eva kalpādāvarkodaye mīnameṣasandhigā bhavanti .
kalpāvasāne ca meṣapraveśe vā bhānorgaganamadhyavartinyāditye dvādaśāṅgulena śaṃkunā samāvanau chāyā grāhyā, tadvargaṃ vyāsārdhavargahate cchāyāśaṃkuvargayogena vibhajet, labdhamakṣajyāvargaḥ .
tatpadamakṣajyā taccāpaṃ svadeśākṣaḥ taṃ rāśitrayādapāsya svadeśāvalambako bhavati .
tajjyāvalambakajyā trijyā vargasya svakrāntivargonasya padaṃ svāharvyāsārdhastasya ca svakāntivaśena dik . svakrāntiviṣuvacchāyāhatā śakuhṛtā kṣitijā, sā trijyāhatā svāharnyāsārdhabhājitā kṣaye vṛddhijyā .
taddhanuścarārdhaṃ vā prāṇāstadghaṭikābhiḥ pañcadaśaghaṭikāyutā dinārdham .
ūnā rātryardhagā evamuttaragolasthā dakṣiṇakāraḥ svasvabhāgāpahāraḥ avāmadhanuṣāmabodhaḥ .
śodhanaṃ vyakṣarāśyudayaprāṇāḥ meṣavṛṣamithunānāṃ krameṇa karkaṭasiṃhakanyānāmutkrameṇa .
meṣavṛṣamidhunajīvādiḥ prāgvaccaraprāṇāḥ kartavyāḥ .
2.34.d:
तात्कालिकशीघ्रं स्फुटं सुपाते योज्यं बुधशुक्रयोः स्वमदाविक्षेपहतां स्फुटान्त्यकर्णेन विभजेत। लब्धं तयोः स्फुटविक्षेपः ।
तात्कालिकस्फुटग्रहस्फुटपातयोगज्यां भौमजीवसौराणां मध्यविक्षेपहतां स्फुटान्त्यकर्णेन विभजेत्, लब्धं तेषां स्फुट विक्षेपः ।
उत्क्रान्तिचापस्फुटविक्षेपयोर्दिशैको योगः तज्जीवस्यक्रान्तिः, तस्या नियोगः शिष्यते सा दिक् तद्गोलस्थश्च ग्रहो भवति ।
एवं ग्रहाणामुत्तरेण दक्षिणेन गतिर्ज्ञेया ।
भचक्रवशेनोदयास्तमयौ कुर्वंतः पश्चिमेन यान्ति ।
पूर्वां व्रजन्तो भगणपरिवर्तान्कुर्वन्ति तत्र च सूर्याश्वपातैः सममेव लङ्कादक्षिणोत्तररेखायाः फाल्गुनान्ते सर्व एव कल्पादावर्कोदये मीनमेषसन्धिगा भवन्ति ।
कल्पावसाने च मेषप्रवेशे वा भानोर्गगनमध्यवर्तिन्यादित्ये द्वादशाङ्गुलेन शंकुना समावनौ छाया ग्राह्या, तद्वर्गं व्यासार्धवर्गहते च्छायाशंकुवर्गयोगेन विभजेत्, लब्धमक्षज्यावर्गः ।
तत्पदमक्षज्या तच्चापं स्वदेशाक्षः तं राशित्रयादपास्य स्वदेशावलम्बको भवति ।
तज्ज्यावलम्बकज्या त्रिज्या वर्गस्य स्वक्रान्तिवर्गोनस्य पदं स्वाहर्व्यासार्धस्तस्य च स्वकान्तिवशेन दिक् । स्वक्रान्तिविषुवच्छायाहता शकुहृता क्षितिजा, सा त्रिज्याहता स्वाहर्न्यासार्धभाजिता क्षये वृद्धिज्या ।
तद्धनुश्चरार्धं वा प्राणास्तद्घटिकाभिः पञ्चदशघटिकायुता दिनार्धम् ।
ऊना रात्र्यर्धगा एवमुत्तरगोलस्था दक्षिणकारः स्वस्वभागापहारः अवामधनुषामबोधः ।
शोधनं व्यक्षराश्युदयप्राणाः मेषवृषमिथुनानां क्रमेण कर्कटसिंहकन्यानामुत्क्रमेण ।
मेषवृषमिधुनजीवादिः प्राग्वच्चरप्राणाः कर्तव्याः ।
2.34.m:
The instantaneous true motion of Mercury and Venus is to be added to their well-computed node; one should divide [the sine of that], multiplied by their own mean inclination, by the true hypotonuse of the apex. The result is their true celestial latitude.
One should multiply the sine of the sum of the instantaneous true planet and true node for Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn by their mean inclination, and divide by the true hypotenuse of the apex; the result is their true celestial latitude.
When the direction of the sine-difference of the arc and the true latitude is the same, their sum is the declination of that sine. Its application remains: that is the direction, and the planet resides in that hemisphere.
In this way, the northward and southward movement of the planets is to be understood.
Causing rising and setting by the force of the starry sphere, they proceed toward the west.
Going toward the east, they perform complete revolutions of the zodiac; and there, together with the nodes of the Sun's horses, precisely on the north-south meridian of Laṅkā at the end of Phālguna, all of them at sunrise at the beginning of the aeon are situated at the junction of Pisces and Aries.
At the end of the aeon, or upon the Sun's entry into Aries, when the Sun is at mid-sky, the shadow should be measured on level ground with a twelve-finger gnomon. One should divide the square of that, multiplied by the square of the radius, by the sum of the squares of the shadow and the gnomon; the result is the square of the sine of latitude.
Its square root is the sine of latitude, and its arc is the terrestrial latitude of one's own locality. Subtracting that from three signs yields the colatitude of one's own locality.
The sine of that is the sine of colatitude. The square root of the square of the radius diminished by the square of one's own declination is the radius of the diurnal circle, and its direction is determined by one's own declination. The sine of one's own declination multiplied by the equinoctial shadow and divided by the gnomon is the earth-sine (kṣitijā). That, multiplied by the radius and divided by the radius of the diurnal circle, is the sine of the ascensional difference in decrease or increase.
Its arc or respiro-moments (prāṇas) is half the ascensional difference. Half the day is [fifteen ghaṭikās] increased by those ghaṭikās [derived from them] added to fifteen ghaṭikās;
diminished by them, it pertains to half the night. Thus for those situated in the northern hemisphere; in the southern hemisphere, it is the reverse deduction of their respective parts, and understanding is without inverse arcs.
The deduction [and] respiro-moments of the rising of the signs at the equator are, in order, for Aries, Taurus, and Gemini, and in reverse order for Cancer, Leo, and Virgo.
The sines and so forth of Aries, Taurus, and Gemini are to be calculated as respiro-moments of the ascensional difference as before.

2.34.s:
